newsitem.title: UK: Irish suspect in London to face extradition.
newsitem.headline: Irish suspect in London to face extradition.

text.p: The daughter of a former Irish republican politician will face a hearing in London on Wednesday to decide whether she should be extradited to Germany to face attempted murder charges, British police said on Tuesday.
Roisin McAliskey, daughter of Bernadette McAliskey, will appear before London's Bow Street magistrates court at 1000 GMT on Wednesday, a police spokesman told Reuters.

"She will face a hearing tomorrow in connection with an attempted murder in Osnabrueck in Germany on or before the 28th of June," the spokesman said. "Officers of the Metropolitan Police extradition squad travelled to Northern Ireland to arrest the woman and escort her to the hearing."
McAliskey, 25, is being held in police custody in London but the spokesman declined to comment on her exact whereabouts.
The charges are linked to an Irish Republican Army (IRA) attack on a British army barracks near the northwest German town of Osnabrueck.

Bernadette Devlin, as she then was, was a leading figure in Northern Irish civil rights marches during the 1960s. She became the youngest woman to be elected to the British parliament when she took her seat on her 22nd birthday in 1969.
She was later jailed for six months for inciting Catholics to riot against the police.
The attack at Osnabrueck was one of the IRA's least successful in its fight to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
Only one of three mortar bombs fired at the barracks exploded and even that fell several yards (metres) short of its intended target, a diesel pump for military vehicles. No one was injured.

The IRA abandoned a 17-month ceasefire in February. It has since set off a series of bombs in Britain, as well as the attack at Osnabrueck and a car bombing at the British army's headquarters in Northern Ireland in which one soldier was killed.
